title.zh: 卷一百八十八 列傳第七十五: 董摶霄 劉哈剌不花 王英 石抹宜孫
title.en: Volume 188 Biographies 75: Dong Tuanxiao, Liuhalabuhua, Wang Ying, Shimoyisun
title.raw: 卷一百八十八 列傳第七十五: 董摶霄 劉哈剌不花 王英 石抹宜孫 Volume 188 Biographies 75: Dong Tuanxiao, Liuhalabuhua, Wang Ying, Shimoyisun

sentences.zh: 董摶霄弟昂霄

translations.literal: Dong Tuanxiao; his younger brother Angxiao
translations.idiomatic: Dong Tuanxiao and His Younger Brother Angxiao

sentences.zh: 董摶霄，字孟起，磁州人。

translations.literal: Dong Tuanxiao, styled Mengqi, was a man of Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Tuanxiao, whose courtesy name was Mengqi, came from Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 由國子生辟陝西行台掾。

translations.literal: From a student of the Imperial Academy he was recruited as a clerk of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Having been a student at the Imperial Academy, he was appointed as a clerk on the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時天大旱，從侍御史郭貞讞獄華陰縣，有李謀兒累殺商賈於道，為賊十五年，至百餘事。

translations.literal: At the time there was a great drought; he followed Censor Guo Zhen in hearing cases at Huayin County. There was one Li Mou'er who had repeatedly killed merchants on the roads, acting as a bandit for fifteen years, with more than a hundred cases.
translations.idiomatic: During a severe drought he accompanied the investigating censor Guo Zhen to try cases in Huayin County, where a man named Li Mou'er had preyed on traveling merchants for fifteen years, his crimes numbering more than a hundred.

sentences.zh: 事覺，獄已具，賄賂有司，謂徒黨未盡獲，五年不決，人皆以為憤。

translations.literal: When the affair came to light the case was complete, but he bribed the officials, claiming his accomplices had not all been captured, and for five years no verdict was rendered; everyone regarded this as outrageous.
translations.idiomatic: Once the crimes were exposed and the case was ready for judgment, he bribed the authorities, insisting that not all his accomplices had been caught, so that for five years no sentence was passed—a source of public outrage.

sentences.zh: 摶霄知之，以言於貞，即以屍諸市中，天乃大雨。

translations.literal: Tuanxiao learned of this and spoke to Zhen about it; Li was immediately exposed as a corpse in the marketplace, and then great rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuanxiao learned of the situation he reported it to Guo Zhen, who had the man executed and his body displayed in the market; rain then poured down in abundance.

sentences.zh: 授四川肅政廉訪司知事，除涇陽縣尹。

translations.literal: He was appointed an associate of the Sichuan Surveillance Commission, then made magistrate of Jingyang County.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted to the Sichuan Surveillance Commission and later appointed magistrate of Jingyang County.

sentences.zh: 入為戶部主事，升員外郎，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: He entered the Ministry of Revenue as a director, was promoted to vice director, and was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the Ministry of Revenue from director to vice director and was then made an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 又出僉遼東肅政廉訪司事，歷江西行省左右司郎中，遷浙東宣慰副使。

translations.literal: He was again sent out as an associate of the Liaodong Surveillance Commission, served as director in the left and right secretariats of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat, and was transferred to be vice commissioner of the Zhedong Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He later served on the Liaodong Surveillance Commission, held directorships in both secretariats of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat, and was promoted to vice commissioner of the Zhedong Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 其歷官所至，往往理冤獄，革弊政，才譽益著稱於時。

translations.literal: Wherever he served in office he often redressed wrongful convictions, reformed corrupt policies, and his talent and reputation grew ever more celebrated in his day.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he held he was known for clearing miscarriages of justice and rooting out abuses, and his ability and reputation steadily won acclaim throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 至正十一年，除濟寧路總管，奉旨從江浙平章教化徵進安豐，兵至合肥定林站，遇賊，大破之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhizheng he was appointed administrator of Jining Circuit; by imperial order he followed the Jiang-Zhe chief minister Jiaohua to advance on Anfeng. When the army reached Dinglin Station in Hefei they encountered bandits and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 11 (1351) he was made administrator of Jining Circuit and, by imperial command, marched with the Jiang-Zhe chief minister Jiaohua to relieve Anfeng; at Dinglin Station near Hefei his troops met the rebels and routed them decisively.

sentences.zh: 時硃皋、固始賊复猖獗，軍少不足以分討。

translations.literal: At that time the rebels at Zhugao and Gushi again grew fierce, and the army was too few to divide for separate campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel activity flared again at Zhugao and Gushi, and government forces were too thin to pursue every front at once.

sentences.zh: 有大山民寨及芍陂屯田軍，摶霄皆獎勞而約束之，遂得障蔽硃皋。

translations.literal: There were mountain militia stockades and the garrison troops of the Shaobo military colonies; Tuanxiao rewarded, encouraged, and disciplined them all, and thus was able to shield Zhugao.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied and disciplined the mountain militia stockades and the Shaobo colony troops, using them to screen the approach to Zhugao.

sentences.zh: 我軍屯硃家寺，賊至，追殺之。

translations.literal: Our army encamped at Zhujia Temple; when bandits came they were pursued and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops encamped at Zhujia Temple, and when rebels appeared they were chased down and slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 乃遣進士程明仲往諭賊中，招徠者千二百家，因悉知其虛實。

translations.literal: He then sent the jinshi Cheng Mingzhong to proclaim terms within the rebel ranks; more than twelve hundred households came over, and thereby he learned their situation in full.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched the jinshi Cheng Mingzhong to negotiate among the rebels, winning over more than twelve hundred households and learning their strength and dispositions in detail.

sentences.zh: 夜縛浮橋於淝水，既渡，賊始覺。

translations.literal: By night they lashed together a pontoon bridge on the Fei River; only after the crossing did the bandits become aware.
translations.idiomatic: Under cover of night they threw a pontoon bridge across the Fei River and crossed before the rebels knew what was happening.

sentences.zh: 賊眾數万據磵南，我軍渡者，輒為其所敗。

translations.literal: Tens of thousands of bandits held the south bank of the stream; those of our army who crossed were repeatedly defeated by them.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of rebels held the far bank, and every detachment that crossed was beaten back.

sentences.zh: 摶霄乃麾騎士，別渡淺灘襲賊後。

translations.literal: Tuanxiao then commanded the horsemen to ford a shallow crossing elsewhere and strike the bandits from the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao then led his cavalry across a shallow ford to hit the rebel rear.

sentences.zh: 賊回東南向，與騎士迎敵，摶霄忽躍馬渡磵，揚言於眾曰：「賊已敗。

translations.literal: The bandits turned southeast to meet the horsemen in battle; Tuanxiao suddenly spurred his horse across the stream and cried out to the host, "The bandits are already defeated."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels wheeled southeast to engage the cavalry; Tuanxiao suddenly leaped his horse across the stream and shouted to the troops, "The enemy is already beaten!"

sentences.zh: 」諸軍皆渡，一鼓而擊之。

translations.literal: " All the armies crossed, and with one drumbeat they struck.
translations.idiomatic: " The whole force crossed at once and attacked with a single roll of the drums.

sentences.zh: 賊大敗，亟追殺之，相藉以死者二十五里，遂復安豐。

translations.literal: The bandits were utterly defeated; he pressed the pursuit and slaughter, with the dead piled upon one another for twenty-five li, and thus recovered Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were shattered; pursuit left corpses heaped along twenty-five li of road, and Anfeng was restored to government control.

sentences.zh: 十二年，有旨命摶霄攻濠州，又命移軍援江南。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year an edict ordered Tuanxiao to attack Haozhou, and also ordered the army shifted to aid the Jiangnan region.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year (1352) he was ordered to attack Haozhou and then to redeploy south to relieve Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 遂渡江，至湖州德清縣，而徽、饒賊已陷杭州。

translations.literal: He then crossed the Yangzi and reached Deqing County in Huzhou, while the Huizhou and Raozhou rebels had already taken Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His force crossed the Yangzi and reached Deqing in Huzhou, only to learn that rebels from Huizhou and Raozhou had already seized Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 教化問摶霄計，摶霄曰：「賊皆野人，見杭城子女玉帛，非平日所有，必縱慾，不暇為備，宜急攻之。

translations.literal: Jiaohua asked Tuanxiao for a plan; Tuanxiao said, "The bandits are all country folk. Seeing the women, children, jade, and silks of Hangzhou—things they never possessed in ordinary days—they are sure to indulge their desires and have no leisure to prepare defenses; we should attack them swiftly."
translations.idiomatic: When Jiaohua asked his advice, Tuanxiao replied, "These rebels are rustics. Confronted with Hangzhou's wealth and women—luxuries they have never known—they will give themselves over to plunder and neglect their defenses. We must strike at once."

sentences.zh: 今欲退保湖州，設使賊乘銳直趨京口，則江南不可為矣。

translations.literal: If we now wish to withdraw and hold Huzhou, suppose the bandits, riding their momentum, press straight to Jingkou—then Jiangnan will be beyond saving.
translations.idiomatic: If we fall back to defend Huzhou and the rebels press their advantage straight to Jingkou, all of Jiangnan will be lost.

sentences.zh: 」教化猶豫未決，而諸將亦難其行。

translations.literal: " Jiaohua hesitated and could not decide, and the generals also found the advance difficult.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiaohua wavered, and the other commanders balked at the proposed advance.

sentences.zh: 摶霄正色曰：「江浙相君方面既陷於賊，今可取而不取，誰任其咎！

translations.literal: Tuanxiao said sternly, "The Jiang-Zhe chief minister's entire jurisdiction has fallen to bandits; if it can now be retaken and we do not retake it, who will bear the blame!"
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao said gravely, "The chief minister's whole territory lies in rebel hands. If we can recover it now and refuse, who will answer for that failure?"

sentences.zh: 」复拔劍顧諸將曰：「諸君荷國厚恩，而臨難苟免，今相君在是，敢有慢令者斬。

translations.literal: " He again drew his sword and turned to the generals, saying, "You gentlemen have received the state's deep favor, yet at peril you seek only to escape. The chief minister is here now—whoever dares disobey orders shall be beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: " He drew his sword and faced the officers: "You owe the dynasty a great debt, yet in danger you think only of saving yourselves. The chief minister is present; anyone who disobeys will be executed."

sentences.zh: 」計乃決。

translations.literal: " The plan was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: " At that the decision was made.

sentences.zh: 遂進兵杭城。

translations.literal: They then advanced on Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The army marched on Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊迎敵，至鹽橋，摶霄麾壯士突前，斬殺數級，而諸軍相繼夾擊之，凡七戰，追殺​​至清河坊。

translations.literal: The bandits came out to meet them; at Salt Bridge Tuanxiao directed picked warriors to charge ahead, beheading several ranks, while the armies in succession attacked from both sides. In all there were seven battles, and pursuit and slaughter reached Qinghe Ward.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels met them in battle; at Salt Bridge Tuanxiao sent elite troops forward, cutting down enemy ranks while the main force closed in from both flanks. After seven engagements the pursuit reached Qinghe Ward.

sentences.zh: 賊奔接待寺，塞其門而焚之，賊皆死，遂復杭州。

translations.literal: The bandits fled to Jiedai Temple, blocked its gates, and set it afire; the bandits all perished, and thus Hangzhou was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels retreated into Jiedai Temple, barred the doors, and set the building ablaze, perishing to the last man; Hangzhou was restored.

sentences.zh: 已而餘杭、武康、德清次第以平，摶霄亦受代去。

translations.literal: Before long Yuhang, Wukang, and Deqing were pacified in turn, and Tuanxiao also completed his term of office and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuhang, Wukang, and Deqing were soon pacified in succession, after which Tuanxiao was relieved and left his post.

sentences.zh: 徽、饒賊復自昱嶺關寇於潛，行省乃假摶霄為參知政事，俾复提兵討之。

translations.literal: The Huizhou and Raozhou bandits again raided Yuqian through Yuling Pass; the Branch Secretariat thereupon provisionally appointed Tuanxiao as vice administrator and ordered him again to lead troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizhou and Raozhou rebels again invaded Yuqian through Yuling Pass, the Branch Secretariat named Tuanxiao acting vice administrator and sent him back at the head of an army.

sentences.zh: 摶霄曰：「必欲除殘去暴，所不敢辭。

translations.literal: Tuanxiao said, "If you truly wish to eliminate the cruel and remove the violent, I dare not refuse."
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao replied, "If the task is to destroy the cruel and suppress the violent, I will not decline it."

sentences.zh: 若假以重爵，則不​​敢受。

translations.literal: If you grant me a lofty title in name, I dare not accept it."
translations.idiomatic: But if you offer me only a grand title, I cannot accept that."

sentences.zh: 」即日引兵至臨安新溪，是為入杭要路，既分兵守之而始進兵至叫口及虎檻，遇賊，皆大破之，追殺至於潛，遂復其縣治。

translations.literal: " That same day he led troops to Xinxie in Lin'an—the vital route into Hangzhou—posted detachments to hold it, and only then advanced to Jiaokou and Hujian, where he met bandits and defeated them all greatly, pursuing and killing as far as Yuqian and restoring its county seat.
translations.idiomatic: " That same day he marched to Xinxie in Lin'an, the key approach to Hangzhou, garrisoned it, and then pushed on to Jiaokou and Hujian, routing every rebel force he met and driving the pursuit to Yuqian, where he restored the county administration.

sentences.zh: 既又克復昌化縣及昱嶺關，降賊將潘大ＣＯ二千人。

translations.literal: He then also recovered Changhua County and Yuling Pass, and the bandit commander Pan Da'ao surrendered with two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He next recovered Changhua County and Yuling Pass, and the rebel leader Pan Da'ao came over with two thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 賊又有犯千秋關者，摶霄還軍守於潛，而賊兵大至，焚倚郭廬舍。

translations.literal: Bandits again attacked Qianqiu Pass; Tuanxiao returned his army to hold Yuqian, and the bandit forces came in great numbers, burning the suburbs outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels struck at Qianqiu Pass, Tuanxiao pulled back to defend Yuqian; the enemy came in force and burned the outlying settlements.

sentences.zh: 摶霄按軍不動，左右請出兵，摶霄曰：「未也。

translations.literal: Tuanxiao held his army motionless; those at his side asked to sally forth, and Tuanxiao said, "Not yet."
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao kept his troops still; his officers urged an attack, but he said, "Not yet."

sentences.zh: 」遣人執白旗登山望賊，約曰：「賊以我為怯，必少懈；

translations.literal: " He sent men bearing white flags up the mountain to watch the bandits, with the agreement: "The bandits will think us timid and must relax somewhat;"
translations.idiomatic: " He posted men with white flags on the heights to watch the enemy, instructing them, "The rebels will take us for cowards and grow careless;"

sentences.zh: 伺其有間，則麾所執旗。

translations.literal: when they see an opening, they are to wave the flags they hold.
translations.idiomatic: when you see an opening, wave your flags."

sentences.zh: 」又伏兵城外，皆授以火砲，复約曰：「見旗動，砲即發。

translations.literal: " He also hid troops outside the walls, all supplied with fire-lances, and again agreed: "When the flags move, the lances fire at once."
translations.idiomatic: " He also hid troops outside the walls with fire-lances, with orders to open fire the moment the flags moved.

sentences.zh: 」已而旗動，砲發，兵乃盡出，斬首數知級，遂復千秋關。

translations.literal: " Before long the flags moved, the lances fired, and the troops all sallied forth, beheading several thousand ranks, and thus Qianqiu Pass was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon the flags waved, the lances roared, and the whole garrison charged out, taking several thousand heads and recovering Qianqiu Pass.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊復攻獨松、百丈、幽嶺三關，摶霄乃先以兵守多溪。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits again attacked the three passes of Dusong, Baizhang, and Youling; Tuanxiao first stationed troops to hold Duoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebels assaulted the passes at Dusong, Baizhang, and Youling; Tuanxiao first secured Duoxi.

sentences.zh: 多溪，三關要路也。

translations.literal: Duoxi was the vital route of the three passes.
translations.idiomatic: Duoxi commanded the approaches to all three passes.

sentences.zh: 既又分為三軍：一出獨松，一出百丈，一出幽嶺。

translations.literal: He then again divided into three armies: one out from Dusong, one from Baizhang, one from Youling.
translations.idiomatic: He then split his force three ways, sending columns through Dusong, Baizhang, and Youling.

sentences.zh: 然後會兵搗賊巢，遂乘勝復安吉，七戰而克之，賊將以其徒來降者數百人。

translations.literal: Afterward he united the armies to strike the bandit lair, then riding the victory recovered Anji; in seven battles he took it, and bandit commanders came over with their followers—several hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: The columns then converged on the rebel stronghold, swept forward to retake Anji after seven engagements, and received the surrender of several hundred rebel fighters with their leaders.

sentences.zh: 既數日，賊復來窺獨松。

translations.literal: Several days later the bandits again came to probe Dusong.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later the rebels probed Dusong again.

sentences.zh: 摶霄即以兵守苦嶺及黃沙嶺。

translations.literal: Tuanxiao immediately stationed troops to hold Kuling and Huangsha Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao at once garrisoned Kuling and Huangsha Ridge.

sentences.zh: 賊帥梅元來降，且言復有帥十一人欲降者，即遣偏將餘思忠至賊寨諭之。

translations.literal: The bandit chief Mei Yuan came to surrender, and also said that eleven more chiefs wished to surrender; he immediately sent the deputy commander Yu Sizhong to the bandit stockade to proclaim terms.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leader Mei Yuan submitted and reported that eleven other chiefs were ready to defect; Tuanxiao sent Deputy Commander Yu Sizhong to their camp to accept their surrender.

sentences.zh: 賊皆入暗室潛議，思忠持火投入室內，拔劍語眾曰：「元帥命我來活汝，汝復何議！

translations.literal: The bandits all entered a dark room to deliberate in secret; Sizhong carried fire and threw it into the room, drew his sword, and said to the crowd, "The marshal ordered me to spare your lives—what more is there to discuss!"
translations.idiomatic: The rebels withdrew to a back room to plot; Sizhong hurled a torch inside, drew his sword, and shouted, "The marshal sent me to spare you—what is left to debate?"

sentences.zh: 」已而火起，焚其寨，叱賊黨散去，而引賊帥來降。

translations.literal: " Before long fire rose and burned their stockade; he shouted at the bandit factions to disperse and led the bandit chiefs in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: " Flames engulfed the camp; he drove the rebel bands apart and escorted their chiefs in to submit.

sentences.zh: 明日，進兵廣德，克之。

translations.literal: The next day he advanced on Guangde and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: The following day his army marched on Guangde and took the city.

sentences.zh: 有蘄賊與饒、池諸賊复犯徽州。

translations.literal: There were Qizhou bandits together with the bandits of Raozhou, Chizhou, and others who again invaded Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels from Qizhou joined forces with those of Raozhou and Chizhou to attack Huizhou again.

sentences.zh: 賊中有道士，能作十二里霧。

translations.literal: Among the bandits was a Daoist priest who could raise a twelve-li fog.
translations.idiomatic: Among them was a Daoist who could conjure a fog twelve li across.

sentences.zh: 摶霄以兵擊之，已而妖霧開豁，諸伏兵皆起，襲賊兵後，賊大潰亂，斬首數万級，擒千餘人。

translations.literal: Tuanxiao attacked them with troops; before long the demonic fog cleared, all the hidden troops rose, and struck the bandit army from the rear; the bandits fell into great rout, heads cut numbered in the tens of thousands, and more than a thousand were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao engaged them; when the sorcerous mist lifted, his ambushers rose and struck the rebel rear, shattering the enemy—tens of thousands were beheaded and more than a thousand taken alive.

sentences.zh: 獲道士，焚其妖書而斬之。

translations.literal: The priest was captured; his sorcerous writings were burned and he was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist was seized, his occult texts burned, and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 遂平徽州。

translations.literal: Thus Huizhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Huizhou was thereby pacified.

sentences.zh: 十四年，除水軍都萬戶。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed commander of the Naval Forces Command.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year (1354) he was made commander of the naval forces.

sentences.zh: 俄升樞密院判官，從丞相脫脫徵高郵，分戍鹽城、興化。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and followed the chief councillor Toghto to campaign against Gaoyou, posting garrisons at Yancheng and Xinghua.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and marched with Chief Councillor Toghto against Gaoyou, stationing detachments at Yancheng and Xinghua.

sentences.zh: 賊巢在大縱、德勝兩湖間，凡十有二，悉剿平之。

translations.literal: Bandit lairs lay between the two lakes of Dazong and Desheng—twelve in all—and all were exterminated and pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve rebel strongholds between Lake Dazong and Lake Desheng were wiped out one after another.

sentences.zh: 即其地築芙蓉寨，賊入，輒迷故道，盡殺之，自是不復敢犯。

translations.literal: On that ground he built Furong Stockade; when bandits entered they always lost their former paths and were all killed, and from then on they no longer dared to invade.
translations.idiomatic: He built Furong Stockade on the site; rebels who entered lost their way and were slaughtered, and afterward none dared approach again.

sentences.zh: 賊恃習水，渡淮北，據安東州。

translations.literal: The bandits, relying on their skill in water, crossed north of the Huai and seized Andong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled on the water, the rebels crossed north of the Huai and seized Andong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 摶霄招善水戰者五百人，與賊戰安東之大湖，大敗之，遂復安東。

translations.literal: Tuanxiao recruited five hundred men skilled in naval combat and fought the bandits on the great lake of Andong, inflicting a great defeat, and thus recovered Andong.
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao raised five hundred expert sailors, met the rebels on Andong's great lake, routed them, and restored the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十六年，剿平北沙、廟灣、沙浦等寨。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he exterminated and pacified the stockades of Beisha, Miaowan, Shapu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year (1356) he cleared the rebel stockades at Beisha, Miaowan, Shapu, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 尋進兵泗州，不利。

translations.literal: Soon he advanced on Sizhou Prefecture, without success.
translations.idiomatic: He then advanced on Sizhou but met with no success.

sentences.zh: 賊乘勝東下，斷我軍糧道，乃回軍屯北沙，糧且絕，與賊死戰，凡七晝夜。

translations.literal: The bandits, riding their victory, pressed east and cut our army's supply route; he therefore returned the army to encamp at Beisha, grain was nearly exhausted, and they fought the bandits to the death for seven days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pressed their advantage eastward and severed his supply line; he fell back to Beisha, where provisions ran out and his men fought to the death for seven days and nights.

sentences.zh: 賊敗走，奪賊船七十餘，乃得渡淮，保泗州。

translations.literal: The bandits were defeated and fled; more than seventy bandit boats were seized, and only then could they cross the Huai and hold Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels broke and fled; seizing more than seventy of their boats, his force crossed the Huai and held Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 時方暑雨，湖水溢，諸營皆避去，而摶霄獨守孤城，賊環繞數十里攻之。

translations.literal: At the time it was the season of summer rains and the lake waters overflowed; all the camps withdrew, while Tuanxiao alone held the isolated city as bandits surrounded it for several tens of li in attack.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer rains the lakes rose and other camps withdrew, but Tuanxiao alone held the isolated city while rebels invested it for miles around.

sentences.zh: 摶霄坐城上，遣偏將以騎士由四門突出賊後，約曰：「旗一麾即還。

translations.literal: Tuanxiao sat atop the wall and sent a deputy commander with horsemen to burst out through the four gates behind the bandits, with the agreement: "At one wave of the flag, return."
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao took his post on the wall and sent cavalry out through all four gates to strike the rebel rear, with orders to return at a single wave of the flag.

sentences.zh: 」既而旗動，騎士還，步卒自城中出，夾擊之，賊大敗。

translations.literal: " When the flag moved the horsemen returned, infantry sallied from within the city, and attacking from both sides they inflicted a great defeat on the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: " When the signal came the cavalry wheeled back and infantry poured out of the gates; caught between the two wings, the rebels were routed.

sentences.zh: 然賊寨猶阻西行之路，乃結陣而往，翊以奇兵，轉戰數十合，軍始得至海寧。

translations.literal: Yet bandit stockades still blocked the road west; he therefore formed battle lines and advanced, supported by surprise troops, fighting several tens of engagements before the army at last reached Haining.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel camps still blocked the westward route; he marched in battle order with flanking detachments, fighting dozens of skirmishes before reaching Haining.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉其功，升同僉淮南行樞密院事。

translations.literal: The court praised his merit and promoted him to associate director of the Huainan Branch Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The court commended his service and promoted him to associate director of the Huainan Branch Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 摶霄建議於朝曰：

translations.literal: Tuanxiao submitted a proposal to the court, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao memorialized the court as follows:

sentences.zh: 淮安為南北襟喉、江淮要沖之地，其地一失，兩淮皆未易復也。

translations.literal: Huai'an is the throat connecting north and south and a vital crossing of the Jiang and Huai; once that place is lost, both banks of the Huai will not be easy to recover.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'an is the strategic hinge between north and south and the vital crossing of the Yangzi and Huai regions; if it falls, both Huai banks will be hard to win back.

sentences.zh: 則救援淮安，誠為急務。

translations.literal: Therefore to relieve Huai'an is truly an urgent task.
translations.idiomatic: Relieving Huai'an must therefore be treated as urgent.

sentences.zh: 為今日計，莫若於黃河上下，並瀕淮海之地，及南自沭陽，北抵沂、莒、贛榆諸州縣，布連珠營，每三十里設一總寨，就三十里中又設一小寨，使斥堠烽燧相望，而巡邏往來，遇賊則並力野戰，無事則屯種而食。

translations.literal: For the present plan, nothing is better than along the upper and lower Yellow River, together with the lands bordering the Huai and sea, and from Shuyang in the south northward to the prefectures and counties of Yi, Ju, and Ganyu, deploying linked-bead camps: every thirty li establishing one main stockade, and within those thirty li again setting one small stockade, so that scouts and beacon fires face one another, patrols come and go, when bandits are met they join strength in field battle, and when there is no affair they garrison, plant, and eat.
translations.idiomatic: For present purposes I propose a chain of fortified camps along the Yellow River and the Huai coast, from Shuyang in the south to Yi, Ju, and Ganyu in the north—a main stockade every thirty li with smaller posts between them, beacon towers in sight of one another, and patrols on constant rotation. When rebels appear, neighboring garrisons unite for battle; in quiet times the troops farm their own provisions.

sentences.zh: 然後進有援，退有守，此善戰者所以常為不可勝，以待敵之可勝也。

translations.literal: Only then in advance there is support and in retreat there is defense—this is why skilled warriors are constantly made invincible, waiting for the enemy to become vulnerable.
translations.idiomatic: Thus every advance will have support and every retreat a refuge—the way a skilled commander keeps himself unbeatable while waiting for the enemy to become beatable.

sentences.zh: 又海寧一境，不通舟楫，軍糧惟可陸運，而凡瀕淮海之地，人民屢經盜賊，宜加存撫，權令軍人搬運。

translations.literal: Moreover the territory of Haining does not admit boats and oars; military grain can only be transported by land. As for all lands bordering the Huai and sea, the people have repeatedly suffered bandits and should receive added relief and nurture; for the time being soldiers should be ordered to carry supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Haining cannot be supplied by water and must rely on overland transport. The coastal Huai region has been ravaged repeatedly; its people need relief, and for the present soldiers should be detailed to carry grain.

sentences.zh: 其陸運之方，每人行十步，三十六人可行一里，三百六十人可行一十里，三千六百人可行一百里。

translations.literal: The method of land transport: each man advances ten paces; thirty-six men can cover one li, three hundred sixty men ten li, and three thousand six hundred men one hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: For overland supply, each carrier advances ten paces before handing off: thirty-six men span one li, three hundred sixty span ten li, and three thousand six hundred span one hundred li.

sentences.zh: 每人負米四斗，以夾布囊盛之，用印封識，人不息肩，米不著地，排列成行，日行五百回，計路二十八里，輕行一十四里，重行一十四里，日可運米二百石。

translations.literal: Each man bears four dou of grain, stored in double cloth sacks, sealed with official stamps; men do not rest their shoulders, grain does not touch the ground, arranged in rows; in one day five hundred circuits are made, reckoning the route at twenty-eight li—fourteen li going light and fourteen li returning heavy—and in a day two hundred shi of grain can be transported.
translations.idiomatic: Each man carries four dou in a double sack, sealed with an official stamp, passing the load from shoulder to shoulder without letting grain touch the ground. Five hundred relays a day—fourteen li outbound empty, fourteen li inbound loaded—would move two hundred shi of grain daily.

sentences.zh: 每運給米一升，可供二萬人。

translations.literal: For each transport, one sheng of grain supplied can feed twenty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Each shi transported provides one sheng per man—enough to sustain twenty thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 此百里一日運糧之術也。

translations.literal: This is the technique of transporting grain one hundred li in one day.
translations.idiomatic: That is how to move grain one hundred li in a single day.

sentences.zh: 又江淮流移之民，並安東、海寧、沭陽、贛榆等州縣俱廢，其民壯者既為軍，老弱無所依歸者，宜設置軍民防禦司，擇軍官材堪牧守者，使居其職，而籍其民，以屯故地。

translations.literal: Moreover the displaced people of the Jiang and Huai, together with the prefectures and counties of Andong, Haining, Shuyang, Ganyu, and others—all abolished—their able-bodied men having already become soldiers, while the old and weak have nowhere to depend or return, ought to have a Military-Civilian Defense Office established, choosing officers whose talent suffices for governing and guarding to hold those posts, registering the people, and settling them to garrison their former lands.
translations.idiomatic: The displaced population of the Jiang-Huai region, together with the abandoned prefectures of Andong, Haining, Shuyang, and Ganyu, also needs care. Able-bodied men are already in the ranks; the old and weak have nowhere to go. Establish a military-civilian defense office, appoint officers fit to govern, register the people, and resettle them on their former lands.

sentences.zh: 於是練兵積穀，且耕且戰，內全山東完固之邦，外禦淮海出沒之寇，而後恢復可圖也。

translations.literal: Thereby training troops and accumulating grain, both farming and fighting, within preserving the intact state of Shandong, without defending against the bandits that appear and vanish on the Huai and sea—and only afterward may recovery be contemplated.
translations.idiomatic: With trained troops and stored grain, farming in peace and fighting in war, we can secure Shandong within and hold the Huai coast without—only then will recovery become possible.

sentences.zh: 十七年，毛貴陷益都、般陽等路，有旨命摶霄從知樞密院事卜蘭奚討之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Mao Gui took Yidu, Banyang, and other circuits; an edict ordered Tuanxiao to follow the Bureau of Military Affairs director Bolanxi to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year (1357) Mao Gui seized Yidu, Banyang, and other circuits; the court ordered Tuanxiao to join Bureau Director Bolanxi in suppressing him.

sentences.zh: 而濟南又告急，摶霄乃提兵援濟南。

translations.literal: But Jinan again reported emergency, and Tuanxiao thereupon led troops to relieve Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Jinan then sent urgent appeals for help, and Tuanxiao marched to its relief.

sentences.zh: 賊眾自南山來攻濟南，望之兩山皆赤。

translations.literal: The bandit host came from the southern mountains to attack Jinan; gazing from afar, both mountains were red.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel horde descended from the southern hills upon Jinan; from a distance both slopes seemed awash in red.

sentences.zh: 摶霄按兵城中，先以數十騎挑之，賊眾悉來鬥，騎兵少卻，至磵上，伏兵起，遂合戰，城中兵又大出，大破之。

translations.literal: Tuanxiao held his army in the city, first sending several tens of horsemen to provoke them; the bandit host all came to fight, the horsemen slightly withdrew to the stream bank, hidden troops rose, and they joined battle; troops from within the city also poured out greatly, and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao kept his main force in the city and sent a few dozen horsemen to bait the enemy. When the whole rebel host engaged, the cavalry feigned retreat to a stream, where ambushers sprang up; government troops then poured from the gates and shattered the rebels.

sentences.zh: 而般陽賊复約泰安之黨，逾南山來襲濟南。

translations.literal: The Banyang bandits again joined with the Taian faction, crossed the southern mountains, and came to raid Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Banyang rebels then allied with Taian bands and crossed the southern hills to strike Jinan again.

sentences.zh: 摶霄列兵城上，弗為動。

translations.literal: Tuanxiao arrayed troops atop the wall and did not move.
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao lined his men along the walls and held his ground.

sentences.zh: 賊夜攻南門，獨以矢石御之。

translations.literal: At night the bandits attacked the south gate; he defended it solely with arrows and stones.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels assaulted the south gate by night; he met them with arrows and stones alone.

sentences.zh: 黎明，乃默開東門，放兵出賊後。

translations.literal: At dawn he silently opened the east gate and released troops behind the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he quietly opened the east gate and sent troops around the rebel rear.

sentences.zh: 既旦，城上兵皆下，大開南門合擊之，賊敗走。

translations.literal: Once it was full day, the troops on the wall all descended, the south gate was opened wide, and they joined in striking; the bandits were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When day broke the men on the walls descended, the south gate swung wide, and the garrison struck from both sides; the rebels broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 复追殺之，賊眾悉無遺者。

translations.literal: He again pursued and killed them; of the bandit host none were left.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued and slaughtered them until not one rebel remained.

sentences.zh: 於是濟南始寧。

translations.literal: Only then did Jinan first become tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Only then was Jinan secure.

sentences.zh: 詔就升淮南行樞密院副使，兼山東宣慰使都元帥，仍賜上尊、金帶、楮幣、名馬以勞之。

translations.literal: An edict immediately promoted him to vice director of the Huainan Branch Bureau of Military Affairs and concurrently commander-in-chief of the Shandong Pacification Commission, still bestowing fine wine, a gold belt, paper currency, and a famous horse to reward his labors.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted on the spot to vice director of the Huainan Branch Bureau of Military Affairs and commander-in-chief of the Shandong Pacification Commission, with gifts of fine wine, a gold belt, paper money, and a prized horse in recognition of his service.

sentences.zh: 有疾其功者，譖於總兵太尉紐的該，令摶霄依前詔，從卜蘭奚同徵益都。

translations.literal: There were those who resented his achievements; they slandered him to the commander-in-chief Grand Marshal Niutachai, ordering Tuanxiao according to the former edict to follow Bolanxi in jointly campaigning against Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Envious rivals slandered him to Grand Marshal Niutachai, who ordered him to leave Jinan and rejoin Bolanxi's campaign against Yidu as originally commanded.

sentences.zh: 摶霄即出濟南城，屬老且病，請以其弟昂霄代領其眾，朝廷從之。

translations.literal: Tuanxiao immediately left Jinan city; as he was old and ill, he requested that his younger brother Angxiao replace him in leading the host, and the court consented.
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao departed Jinan; aged and ill, he asked that his younger brother Angxiao take command of his troops, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 授昂霄淮南行樞密院判官。

translations.literal: Angxiao was appointed vice director of the Huainan Branch Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Angxiao was appointed vice director of the Huainan Branch Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 未幾，有旨命摶霄守河間之長蘆。

translations.literal: Before long an edict ordered Tuanxiao to guard Changlu in Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was ordered to defend Changlu in Hejian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十八年，摶霄以兵北行，且曰：「我去，濟南必不可保。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Tuanxiao marched north with troops, saying, "When I leave, Jinan surely cannot be preserved."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year (1358) he marched north and warned, "Once I am gone, Jinan cannot be held."

sentences.zh: 」既而濟南果陷。

translations.literal: " Before long Jinan indeed fell.
translations.idiomatic: " Jinan soon fell, just as he had foretold.

sentences.zh: 摶霄方駐兵南皮縣之魏家莊，適有使者奉詔拜摶霄河南行省右丞，甫拜命，毛貴兵已至，而營壘猶未完。

translations.literal: Tuanxiao was just then encamped at Weijiazhuang in Nanpi County when an envoy arrived with an edict appointing him right vice minister of the Henan Branch Secretariat; he had barely accepted the commission when Mao Gui's troops were already upon them, and the camp fortifications were still unfinished.
translations.idiomatic: While he was encamped at Weijiazhuang in Nanpi County, an envoy arrived to appoint him right vice minister of the Henan Branch Secretariat. He had scarcely taken the commission when Mao Gui's army appeared, and the camp was not yet fortified.

sentences.zh: 諸將謂摶霄曰：「賊至當如何？

translations.literal: The generals said to Tuanxiao, "When the bandits arrive, what shall we do?"
translations.idiomatic: His officers asked, "What are we to do when the enemy arrives?"

sentences.zh: 」摶霄曰：「我受命至此，當以死報國耳。

translations.literal: " Tuanxiao said, "Having received my commission to come here, I ought to repay the state with my death, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: " Tuanxiao replied, "I was sent here to serve the dynasty; I can only repay that trust with my life."

sentences.zh: 」因拔劍督兵以戰。

translations.literal: " He thereupon drew his sword and urged the troops into battle.
translations.idiomatic: " He drew his sword and led his men into the fight.

sentences.zh: 而賊眾突至摶霄前，捽而問曰：「汝為誰？

translations.literal: The bandit host suddenly rushed before Tuanxiao, seized him, and asked, "Who are you?"
translations.idiomatic: Rebel soldiers burst upon him, seized him, and demanded, "Who are you?"

sentences.zh: 」摶霄曰：「我董老爺也！

translations.literal: " Tuanxiao said, "I am Lord Dong!"
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "I am Lord Dong!"

sentences.zh: 」眾刺殺之，無血，惟見其有白氣沖天。

translations.literal: " The crowd stabbed and killed him; no blood flowed, and only a white vapor was seen rushing to the sky.
translations.idiomatic: " They stabbed him to death; no blood appeared, and witnesses saw only a white vapor rise into the sky.

sentences.zh: 是日，昂霄亦死之。

translations.literal: That same day Angxiao also died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Angxiao fell the same day.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈宣忠守正保節功臣、榮祿大夫、河南行省平章政事、柱國，追封魏國公，諡忠定。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously granted the title of Meritorious Minister for Loyalty, Integrity, and Preservation of Integrity, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, chief minister of the Henan Branch Secretariat, and Pillar of the State, posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Wei, with the posthumous name Zhongding.
translations.idiomatic: When news of his death reached the court, he was posthumously honored as Duke of Wei with the temple name Zhongding and given the ranks of chief minister of the Henan Branch Secretariat and Pillar of the State.

sentences.zh: 昂霄贈推誠孝節功臣、嘉議大夫、禮部尚書、上輕車都尉，追封隴西郡侯，諡忠毅。

translations.literal: Angxiao was posthumously granted Meritorious Minister for Sincerity, Filial Piety, and Integrity, Grand Master for Glorious Discussion, Minister of Rites, and Superior Commandant of Light Chariots, posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Longxi Commandery, with the posthumous name Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: Angxiao was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Longxi with the temple name Zhongyi and honored as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 摶霄早以儒生起家，輒為能吏，會天下大亂，乃復以武功自奮，其才略有大過人者，而當時用之不能盡其才，君子惜之。

translations.literal: Tuanxiao early rose from the Confucian scholar class and was forthwith an able official; when the empire fell into great disorder he again exerted himself through military achievement. His talent and strategy greatly surpassed other men, yet those who employed him at the time could not exhaust his ability—men of discernment regretted this.
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao had begun as a Confucian scholar and proved an outstanding administrator; when the realm collapsed into chaos he distinguished himself in war as well. His abilities far exceeded those around him, yet the court never fully used them—a loss that thoughtful men deplored.

sentences.zh: ○劉哈剌不花

translations.literal: ○ Liu Halabuhua
translations.idiomatic: Liu Halabuhua

sentences.zh: 劉哈剌不花，其先江西人。

translations.literal: Liu Halabuhua—his ancestors were men of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Halabuhua's family came originally from Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 倜儻好義，不事家產，有古俠士風。

translations.literal: Unconventional and fond of righteousness, he did not attend to family property and had the air of an ancient knight-errant.
translations.idiomatic: Free-spirited and devoted to justice, he cared little for wealth and bore the manner of an old-fashioned knight-errant.

sentences.zh: 居燕趙有年，遂為探馬赤軍戶。

translations.literal: He lived in Yan and Zhao for many years and thus became a tamachi military household.
translations.idiomatic: After years in the Yan-Zhao region he was registered as a tamachi military household.

sentences.zh: 至正十二年，潁、亳盜起，朝遷以泰不花為河南行省平章政事，總兵討之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhizheng bandits rose at Ying and Bo; the court transferred Toqto'a to be chief minister of the Henan Branch Secretariat and placed him in overall command to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 12 (1352) rebels broke out in Ying and Bo prefectures; the court appointed Toqto'a chief minister of the Henan Branch Secretariat and gave him overall command of the campaign.

sentences.zh: 哈剌不花上書陳十事，其七言兵機及攻守方略。

translations.literal: Halabuhua submitted a memorial setting forth ten matters, seven of which concerned military opportunity and offensive and defensive strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Halabuhua memorialized the throne with ten proposals, seven of them on military timing and strategy.

sentences.zh: 泰不花大喜，即辟為掾史。

translations.literal: Toqto'a was greatly pleased and immediately recruited him as a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Toqto'a was delighted and took him on as a staff clerk.

sentences.zh: 未幾，奏除左右司都事。

translations.literal: Before long he was memorialized for appointment as director of the left and right secretariats.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to director in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 泰不花以哈剌不花嘗為探馬赤，有膂力，善騎射，俾統前八翼軍，為先鋒將。

translations.literal: Toqto'a, because Halabuhua had once been a tamachi, possessed great physical strength, and was skilled in horsemanship and archery, ordered him to command the forward eight-wing army as vanguard general.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Halabuhua's tamachi background, strength, and mastery of horsemanship and archery, Toqto'a put him in command of the vanguard of the forward eight-wing army.

sentences.zh: 明號令，信賞罰，士皆樂為之用，而料敵成敗，所向無失。

translations.literal: He made orders clear, trusted in rewards and punishments, and soldiers all gladly served under him; in estimating the enemy's success or failure, wherever he turned he did not err.
translations.idiomatic: Clear in command and strict in discipline, he won his men's loyalty; in reading the enemy he was seldom wrong.

sentences.zh: 是時，答失八都魯軍潰於長葛，收集散卒，复屯中牟。

translations.literal: At this time Dashi Badulu's army was routed at Changge; he gathered scattered soldiers and again encamped at Zhongmou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Dashi Badulu's army had been routed at Changge; he regrouped the survivors and encamped at Zhongmou.

sentences.zh: 哈剌不花軍於汴梁南彭子岡。

translations.literal: Halabuhua encamped his army at Pengzigang south of Bianliang.
translations.idiomatic: Halabuhua stationed his troops at Pengzigang, south of Bianliang.

sentences.zh: 有自長葛來者言，總兵官已為賊所敗，次中牟。

translations.literal: Someone coming from Changge said the commander-in-chief had already been defeated by bandits and was now at Zhongmou.
translations.idiomatic: A messenger from Changge reported that the commander had been beaten and was falling back on Zhongmou.

sentences.zh: 哈剌不花曰：「賊既捷，兵必再至，我不可不往援。

translations.literal: Halabuhua said, "The bandits having won, their troops are sure to come again—we cannot fail to go to his relief."
translations.idiomatic: Halabuhua said, "With the enemy emboldened by victory, they will strike again—we must go to his aid."

sentences.zh: 」遂整兵而前。

translations.literal: " He thereupon arrayed his troops and advanced.
translations.idiomatic: " He marched out at once.

sentences.zh: 既而有使馳報：夜四鼓，賊從洧川渡河，未知其所向。

translations.literal: Before long a messenger came at full gallop reporting: at the fourth watch of the night the bandits crossed the river from Weichuan, and their direction was unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a courier arrived with urgent news: at the fourth watch rebels had crossed the river from Weichuan, destination unknown.

sentences.zh: 哈剌不花曰：「是必襲答失八都魯營耳。

translations.literal: Halabuhua said, "They are surely raiding Dashi Badulu's camp."
translations.idiomatic: Halabuhua said, "They must be striking Dashi Badulu's camp."

sentences.zh: 我行已緩，不及事，不若以精銳斷賊歸路，覆之必矣。

translations.literal: Our march is already slow and will not reach in time; better to use picked troops to cut off the bandits' line of retreat—overwhelming them is certain."
translations.idiomatic: We are too late to intervene; better to post elite troops on their line of retreat and destroy them when they withdraw."

sentences.zh: 」於是領軍徐行。

translations.literal: " He therefore led the army forward at a deliberate pace.
translations.idiomatic: " He advanced slowly with his main force.

sentences.zh: 天未明，伏軍其歸路。

translations.literal: Before dawn he ambushed troops on their route of return.
translations.idiomatic: Before dawn he laid an ambush along their retreat route.

sentences.zh: 賊果襲答失八都魯營，大掠輜重而回。

translations.literal: The bandits indeed raided Dashi Badulu's camp, plundered baggage heavily, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels did raid Dashi Badulu's camp, looted his baggage train, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 哈剌不花伏軍四起，賊大敗，盡俘獲之。

translations.literal: Halabuhua's hidden troops rose on all sides; the bandits were greatly defeated and all were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Halabuhua's ambushers sprang up on every side; the rebels were crushed and taken to the last man.

sentences.zh: 當是時，答失八都魯雖以平章政事總大兵，而哈剌不花功名與之相埒。

translations.literal: At that time, although Dashi Badulu as chief minister commanded the great army, Halabuhua's achievements and fame were on a par with his.
translations.idiomatic: Though Dashi Badulu held chief ministerial rank and overall command, Halabuhua's reputation now matched his own.

sentences.zh: 十七年，山東毛貴率其賊眾，由河間趨直沽，遂犯漷州，至棗林。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Mao Gui of Shandong led his bandit host from Hejian toward Zhigu, then invaded Huozhou and reached Zaolin.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year (1357) Mao Gui of Shandong marched his rebels from Hejian toward Zhigu, attacked Huozhou, and reached Zaolin.

sentences.zh: 已而略柳林，逼畿甸，樞密副使達國珍戰死，京師人心大駭。

translations.literal: Before long they overran Liulin and pressed upon the capital region; Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Daguo Zhen died in battle, and the hearts of the people in the capital were greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: They then overran Liulin and threatened the capital district; Vice Director Daguo Zhen was killed in battle, and panic seized the court.

sentences.zh: 在廷之臣，或勸乘輿北巡以避之，或勸遷都關陝，眾議紛然，獨左丞相太平執不可。

translations.literal: Ministers at court some urged the imperial carriage to tour north to avoid them, some urged moving the capital to Guanzhong and Shaanxi; opinions were confused and numerous, but only the left chief minister Taiping held that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Some ministers urged the emperor to tour the north to escape the rebels, others to move the capital to the northwest; debate raged, but Left Chief Minister Taiping alone insisted that neither course was acceptable.

sentences.zh: 哈剌不花時為同知樞密院事，奉詔以兵拒之，與之戰於柳林，大捷。

translations.literal: Halabuhua was then associate director of the Bureau of Military Affairs; by imperial order he led troops to resist them and fought them at Liulin, achieving a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: Halabuhua, then associate director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was ordered to meet the invaders and won a decisive victory at Liulin.

sentences.zh: 貴眾悉潰退，走據濟南，京師遂安，哈剌不花之功居多。

translations.literal: Gui's host all broke and retreated, fleeing to hold Jinan; the capital was thereby secured, and Halabuhua's merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Gui's forces collapsed and fled to Jinan; the capital was saved, largely through Halabuhua's efforts.

sentences.zh: 哈剌不花後遷河南行省平章政事以卒。

translations.literal: Halabuhua was later transferred to chief minister of the Henan Branch Secretariat and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to chief minister of the Henan Branch Secretariat and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 初，哈剌不花與信州人倪晦字孟晰同事泰不花為掾史。

translations.literal: Earlier, Halabuhua and Ni Hui of Xinzhou, styled Mengxi, had served together under Toqto'a as clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Halabuhua had served alongside Ni Hui of Xinzhou, styled Mengxi, as a clerk under Toqto'a.

sentences.zh: 晦涉書史，精文墨，機識警敏，泰不花深委任之，言無不從；

translations.literal: Hui was versed in books and histories, skilled in letters, quick and alert in judgment; Toqto'a deeply entrusted affairs to him, and no word of his went unheeded;
translations.idiomatic: Ni Hui was learned, literate, and quick-witted; Toqto'a relied on him completely and followed his counsel in everything;

sentences.zh: 而哈剌不花或有所論白，多沮不行，由是心銜泰不花。

translations.literal: when Halabuhua sometimes offered reports and proposals, they were mostly blocked and not carried out—thereby he harbored resentment in his heart toward Toqto'a.
translations.idiomatic: while Halabuhua's own recommendations were often blocked—an affront that left him resentful toward Toqto'a.

sentences.zh: 及泰不花事敗，走詣哈剌不花求援，而哈剌不花不能曲為保全，乃縛泰不花送京師，致之死地，君子以是少之。

translations.literal: When Toqto'a's affairs failed he fled to seek Halabuhua's aid, but Halabuhua could not bend matters to preserve him; he bound Toqto'a and sent him to the capital, bringing about his death—men of discernment for this held him somewhat in low esteem.
translations.idiomatic: When Toqto'a fell from power he fled to Halabuhua for protection, but Halabuhua would not shield him; he bound Toqto'a and sent him to the capital to his death—a deed that earned him the disapproval of thoughtful men.

sentences.zh: ○王英

translations.literal: ○ Wang Ying
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ying

sentences.zh: 王英，字邦傑，益都人。

translations.literal: Wang Ying, styled Bangjie, was a man of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ying, whose courtesy name was Bangjie, came from Yidu.

sentences.zh: 性剛果，有大節，膂力絕人，善騎射。

translations.literal: By nature he was firm and resolute, possessed of great integrity, with physical strength surpassing other men, and skilled in horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Firm and principled, he possessed extraordinary strength and was a master of horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 襲父職，為莒州翼千戶。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's post and became commander of a wing at Juzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's post as commander of a wing at Juzhou.

sentences.zh: 父子皆善用雙刀，人號之曰刀王。

translations.literal: Father and son were both skilled in the use of paired sabers, and people styled them the Saber Kings.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son were both famed for their paired sabers, and men called them the Saber Kings.

sentences.zh: 至元二十九年，江西行樞密院命帥師南雄，討賊丘大老。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Zhiyuan the Jiangxi Branch Bureau of Military Affairs ordered him to command troops at Nanxiong to suppress the bandit Qiu Dalao.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 29 (1292) the Jiangxi Branch Bureau of Military Affairs sent him to Nanxiong to suppress the bandit Qiu Dalao.

sentences.zh: 賊六百餘人突至，英與戰，殺其渠帥劉把東，獲九十餘人。

translations.literal: More than six hundred bandits suddenly arrived; Ying fought them, killed their chieftain Liu Badong, and captured more than ninety men.
translations.idiomatic: When more than six hundred rebels attacked, he met them in battle, killed their leader Liu Badong, and took more than ninety prisoners.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年，從左丞董士選討大山賊劉貴，擒之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen he followed the left vice minister Dong Shixuan to suppress the Dashan bandit Liu Gui and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanzhen 1 (1295) he joined Vice Minister Dong Shixuan in suppressing the Dashan rebel Liu Gui and took him alive.

sentences.zh: 二年，討永新、安福二州賊，餘黨皆息。

translations.literal: In the second year he suppressed the bandits of Yongxin and Anfu prefectures, and the remaining factions all subsided.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he pacified rebels in Yongxin and Anfu, and their remnants subsided.

sentences.zh: 延祐二年，寧都賊起，行省命英率各萬戶軍討之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanyou bandits rose at Ningdu; the Branch Secretariat ordered Ying to lead the various wanhu armies to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 2 (1315) rebels rose in Ningdu, and the Branch Secretariat ordered Ying to lead the wanhu forces against them.

sentences.zh: 賊勢甚張，英屢戰皆勝，斬獲不可勝數，積尸盈野，水為不流。

translations.literal: The bandit power was very strong; Ying fought repeatedly and always won, beheadings and captures beyond counting, corpses heaped filling the fields, and the waters ceased to flow.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were formidable, but Ying won every engagement; the slain piled the fields so deep that streams were choked with corpses.

sentences.zh: 行省平章李世安，遣英迓江浙平章張閭所領軍於閩境，至木麻坑，擒賊蔡五九。

translations.literal: Branch Secretariat chief minister Li Shi'an dispatched Ying to meet the army led by the Jiang-Zhe chief minister Zhang Lu at the Fujian border; reaching Mumakeng, he captured the bandit Cai Wujiu.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Li Shi'an sent Ying to rendezvous in Fujian with the army of Jiang-Zhe chief minister Zhang Lu; at Mumakeng he captured the rebel Cai Wujiu.

sentences.zh: 又追賊至上虎嶂，遇賊三千餘人，盡殲之。

translations.literal: He again pursued bandits to Shanghuzhang, encountered more than three thousand bandits, and annihilated them all.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued rebels to Shanghuzhang, met three thousand of them, and wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 至治元年，以大臣薦，授忠武校尉、益都淄萊萬戶府副千戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizhi, on the recommendation of a high minister, he was appointed Loyal and Martial Captain and vice commander of the Yidu-Zilai Wanhu Office.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizhi 1 (1321), recommended by a senior minister, he was made Loyal and Martial Captain and vice commander of the Yidu-Zilai Wanhu Office.

sentences.zh: 天曆元年，授宣武將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianli he was appointed Pacifying Martial General.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianli 1 (1328) he was appointed Pacifying Martial General.

sentences.zh: 至順二年，行省命英招捕桂陽州賊張思進等二千人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhishun the Branch Secretariat ordered Ying to recruit and capture the Guiyang Prefecture bandits Zhang Sijin and others—two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhishun 2 (1331) the Branch Secretariat ordered him to bring in Zhang Sijin of Guiyang and two thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 英至，布以威信，皆相率請降。

translations.literal: When Ying arrived he spread authority and trust, and all came forward in succession to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying arrived he won them over with firmness and fairness, and they surrendered in a body.

sentences.zh: 元統元年，授懷遠大將軍、同知海北海南道宣慰使司事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuantong he was appointed Far-Reaching General and associate commissioner of the Haibei-Hainan Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuantong 1 (1333) he was made Far-Reaching General and associate commissioner of the Haibei-Hainan Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 至元三年，萬安軍賊吳汝期等作亂，聚眾三千人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhiyuan the Wan'an Army bandits Wu Ruqi and others rebelled, gathering a host of three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 3 (1343) Wu Ruqi and other rebels in Wan'an Army raised three thousand men in revolt.

sentences.zh: 英至，賊皆就擒。

translations.literal: When Ying arrived the bandits were all captured.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying arrived the rebels were all taken.

sentences.zh: 未幾，李志甫起漳州，劉虎仔起潮州，詔命江西行省右丞燕帖木兒討之。

translations.literal: Before long Li Zhipu rose in Zhangzhou and Liu Huzai rose in Chaozhou; an edict ordered the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat right vice minister El Temür to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Li Zhipu rebelled in Zhangzhou and Liu Huzai in Chaozhou; the court ordered Jiangxi Vice Minister El Temür to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 方賊起時，英已致仕，平章政事伯撒里謂僚佐曰：「是雖鼠竊狗偷，非刀王行不可。

translations.literal: Just as the bandits rose Ying had already retired from office; Chief Minister Baisari said to his staff, "Though these are rats stealing and dogs snatching, without the Saber King going it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels rose, Ying had already retired. Chief Minister Baisari told his staff, "Petty thieves though they may be, only the Saber King can handle this."

sentences.zh: 其人雖投老，必可以義激。

translations.literal: The man, though cast into old age, surely can be roused by righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: He is old, but duty will move him."

sentences.zh: 」乃使迎致之。

translations.literal: " He therefore sent men to welcome and bring him.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent to fetch Ying.

sentences.zh: 英曰：「國家有事，吾雖老，其可坐視乎！

translations.literal: Ying said, "The state has an affair—though I am old, how can I sit and watch!"
translations.idiomatic: Ying said, "The dynasty is in peril; though I am old, how can I stand aside?"

sentences.zh: 」據鞍橫槊，精神飛動，馳赴焉。

translations.literal: " He gripped the saddle and levelled his spear, his spirit soaring, and galloped to join them.
translations.idiomatic: " He seized saddle and spear, his vigor undimmed, and rode to the front.

sentences.zh: 及賊平，英功居多。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, Ying's merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were subdued, the credit belonged chiefly to Ying.

sentences.zh: 至正中，毛貴陷益都，英時年九十有六，乃謂其子弘曰：「我世受國恩，美官厚祿，備嘗享之。

translations.literal: In the Zhizheng period Mao Gui took Yidu; Ying was then ninety-six years old, and he said to his son Hong, "Our family for generations has received the state's grace—fine offices and rich stipends—we have fully tasted and enjoyed them."
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhizheng era Mao Gui seized Yidu. Ying was ninety-six and said to his son Hong, "Our family has enjoyed the dynasty's favor for generations—rank, stipends, and honors in full measure."

sentences.zh: 今老矣，縱不能事戎馬以報天子，尚忍食異姓之粟以求生乎！

translations.literal: Now I am old; even if I cannot serve in arms to repay the Son of Heaven, how could I still bear to eat the grain of another surname to seek life!"
translations.idiomatic: I am old now. Even if I can no longer ride to war for the emperor, how could I eat the rebels' grain to stay alive?"

sentences.zh: 」水漿不入口者數日，遂卒。

translations.literal: " For several days he took neither water nor broth into his mouth, and thus died.
translations.idiomatic: " He refused food and drink for days and died.

sentences.zh: 毛貴聞之，使具棺衾以葬。

translations.literal: When Mao Gui heard of it he had coffin and shroud prepared for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of his death, Mao Gui provided a coffin and shroud for the burial.

sentences.zh: 將斂，舉其屍不動，焚香祝曰：「公子弘請公歸葬先塋。

translations.literal: When they were about to enshroud him they lifted his corpse but it did not move; burning incense they prayed, "Your son Hong asks you, sir, to return for burial in the ancestral grave."
translations.idiomatic: As they prepared the body it could not be lifted; incense was burned and a prayer offered: "Your son Hong begs you to return to the family grave."

sentences.zh: 」祝畢，屍遂起，觀者莫不驚異。

translations.literal: " When the prayer was finished the corpse then rose; none of the onlookers failed to be startled and amazed.
translations.idiomatic: " When the prayer ended the body rose, to the astonishment of all who watched.

sentences.zh: 山東宣慰使普顏不花及憲司請卹典於朝，有曰：「不食寇粟，餓死芹泉，有夷、齊之風，為臣之清者也。

translations.literal: The Shandong Pacification Commissioner Puyan Buhua and the surveillance commission requested mourning rites from the court; someone said, "Refusing to eat the bandits' grain, starving to death at Qinquan—he had the air of Bo Yi and Shu Qi; this is the purity of a minister."
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Puyan Buhua and the surveillance officials petitioned for state mourning honors, noting, "He would not eat rebel grain and starved at Qinquan—conduct worthy of Bo Yi and Shu Qi, the purity of a loyal minister."

sentences.zh: 」芹泉，谷名，英所居也。

translations.literal: " Qinquan was the name of a valley where Ying dwelt.
translations.idiomatic: " Qinquan was the valley where Ying had lived.

sentences.zh: ○石抹宜孫

translations.literal: ○ Shimoyisun
translations.idiomatic: Shimoyisun

sentences.zh: 石抹宜孫，字申之。

translations.literal: Shimoyisun, styled Shenzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shimoyisun, whose courtesy name was Shenzhi.

sentences.zh: 其先遼之迪烈糺人。

translations.literal: His ancestors were Dilieqiu people of the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors were Dilieqiu people of the Liao dynasty.

sentences.zh: 五世祖曰也先，事太祖為御史大夫，自有傳。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor was called Yexian, who served the Taizu as Censor-in-Chief and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Yexian served Taizu as Censor-in-Chief and has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 也先之曾孫曰繼祖，字伯善，襲父職，為沿海上副萬戶。

translations.literal: Yexian's great-grandson was called Jizu, styled Boshan, who inherited his father's post and became vice commander of the Coastal Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yexian's great-grandson Jizu, styled Boshan, inherited his father's post as vice commander of the Coastal Guard.

sentences.zh: 初以沿海軍分鎮台州，皇慶元年，又移鎮婺、處兩州。

translations.literal: At first with coastal troops he was posted to garrison Taizhou; in the first year of Huangqing he was again transferred to garrison the two prefectures of Wu and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: He first garrisoned Taizhou with coastal troops; in Huangqing 1 (1312) he was transferred to garrison Wu and Chu prefectures.

sentences.zh: 馭軍嚴肅，平寧都寇，有戰功；

translations.literal: In commanding troops he was stern and severe, pacified the Ningdu bandits, and had military achievements;
translations.idiomatic: He commanded with strict discipline, pacified the Ningdu rebels, and won distinction in battle;

sentences.zh: 且明達政事，講究鹽策，多合時宜。

translations.literal: moreover he was clear-sighted in government affairs, studied salt policy, and much accorded with the needs of the time.
translations.idiomatic: he was also adept at administration and devised salt policies well suited to the times.

sentences.zh: 為學本於經術，而兼通名法、縱橫、天文、地理、術數、方技、釋老之說，見稱薦紳間。

translations.literal: In learning he rooted himself in the classics, yet was also versed in legalism, coalition strategy, astronomy, geography, numerology, technical arts, and the teachings of Buddhism and Daoism, and was praised among the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: His scholarship rested on the classics, but he also mastered law, statecraft, astronomy, geography, divination, the technical arts, and Buddhist and Daoist learning, earning praise among the gentry.

sentences.zh: 宜孫其子也。

translations.literal: Yisun was his son.
translations.idiomatic: Yisun was his son.

sentences.zh: 宜孫性警敏，嗜學問，於書務博覽，而長於詩歌。

translations.literal: Yisun was by nature alert and keen, fond of learning; in books he aimed at broad reading and excelled in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Yisun was quick-witted and devoted to learning; he read widely and excelled at poetry.

sentences.zh: 嘗借嫡弟厚孫廕，襲父職，為沿海上副萬戶，守處州。

translations.literal: He once borrowed his younger brother Housun's hereditary privilege, inherited his father's post, became vice commander of the Coastal Guard, and guarded Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He once used his younger brother Housun's hereditary privilege to inherit his father's post as vice commander of the Coastal Guard and garrison Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 及弟長，即讓其職還之，退居台州。

translations.literal: When his brother came of age he immediately yielded the post back to him and withdrew to reside in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his brother came of age he returned the post and retired to Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 至正十一年，方國珍起海上，江浙行省檄宜孫守溫州，宜孫即起任其事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhizheng Fang Guozhen rose on the sea; the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat issued an order to Yisun to guard Wenzhou, and Yisun immediately rose to take up the task.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 11 (1351), when Fang Guozhen rose at sea, the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat ordered Yisun to defend Wenzhou, and he took up the post at once.

sentences.zh: 其年閩寇犯處州，复檄宜孫以兵平之。

translations.literal: That same year Fujian bandits invaded Chuzhou; again an order was issued to Yisun to pacify them with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Later that year Fujian rebels attacked Chuzhou, and he was ordered to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 以功升浙東宣慰副使，分府於台州。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted to vice commissioner of the Zhedong Pacification Commission, with his separate office at Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was promoted to vice commissioner of the Zhedong Pacification Commission, with headquarters at Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 頃之，處之屬縣山寇並起，宜孫復奉省檄往討之。

translations.literal: Before long mountain bandits rose together in the subordinate counties of Chu; Yisun again received a Branch Secretariat order to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon mountain rebels rose throughout Chu's subordinate counties, and Yisun was again dispatched to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 至則築處州城，為御敵計。

translations.literal: Upon arrival he built the walls of Chuzhou as a plan to resist the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he fortified Chuzhou city to prepare for enemy attack.

sentences.zh: 十七年，江浙行省左丞相達識鐵睦邇承製升宜孫行樞密院判官，總制處州，分院治於處。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat left chief minister Dash Timur, by provisional appointment, promoted Yisun to vice director of the Branch Bureau of Military Affairs, placing him in overall control of Chuzhou, with a separate office administering from Chu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year (1357) Left Chief Minister Dash Timur appointed Yisun vice director of the Branch Bureau of Military Affairs with overall command of Chuzhou and a separate headquarters there.

sentences.zh: 又以江浙儒學副提舉劉基為其院經歷，蕭山縣尹蘇友龍為照磨，而宜孫又辟郡人胡深、葉琛、章溢參謀其軍事。

translations.literal: He also appointed the Jiang-Zhe vice promoter of Confucian learning Liu Ji as director of his bureau, the Xiaoshan magistrate Su Youlong as registrar, while Yisun further recruited the men of his prefecture Hu Shen, Ye Chen, and Zhang Yi to advise on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Liu Ji director of his staff, Su Youlong registrar, and recruited local men Hu Shen, Ye Chen, and Zhang Yi as military advisers.

sentences.zh: 處為郡，山谷聯絡，盜賊憑據險阻，輒竊發，不易平治。

translations.literal: Chu was a prefecture where valleys and mountains linked together; bandits relied on perilous terrain and repeatedly rose in secret raids, not easy to pacify.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhou's rugged terrain gave bandits natural strongholds from which they struck repeatedly, making pacification difficult.

sentences.zh: 宜孫用基等謀，或搗以兵，或誘以計，未幾，皆殲殄無遺類。

translations.literal: Yisun used the plans of Ji and the others—sometimes striking with troops, sometimes luring with stratagems—and before long all were exterminated without survivors.
translations.idiomatic: Following Liu Ji's counsel, Yisun alternated force and stratagem; soon every bandit band was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 尋升同僉行樞密院事。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to associate director of the Branch Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to associate director of the Branch Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 當是之時，天下已多故，所在守將各自為計相保守。

translations.literal: At that time the empire already had many troubles; garrison commanders everywhere each made plans to preserve themselves.
translations.idiomatic: By then the realm was in turmoil, and local commanders everywhere looked chiefly to their own survival.

sentences.zh: 於是浙東則宜孫在處州，邁里古思在紹興為稱首。

translations.literal: Thus in Zhedong, Yisun was at Chuzhou and Mailigusi at Shaoxing as the foremost figures.
translations.idiomatic: In eastern Zhejiang, Yisun at Chuzhou and Mailigusi at Shaoxing were the leading defenders.

sentences.zh: 十八年十二月，大明兵取蘭溪，且逼婺，而宜孫母實在婺城。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the eighteenth year the Great Ming army took Lanxi and was pressing upon Wu, while Yisun's mother was actually in Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the eighteenth year (1358) Ming forces took Lanxi and advanced on Wu Prefecture, where Yisun's mother was trapped in the city.

sentences.zh: 宜孫泣曰：「義莫重於君親，食祿而不事其事，是無君也；

translations.literal: Yisun wept and said, "In righteousness nothing is heavier than ruler and kin; eating stipend yet not serving the affair—this is being without a ruler;"
translations.idiomatic: Yisun wept and said, "Nothing outweighs duty to ruler and parent. To draw salary yet refuse service is to betray one's lord;"

sentences.zh: 母在難而不赴，是無親也。

translations.literal: when one's mother is in peril yet one does not go—this is being without kin."
translations.idiomatic: to leave one's mother in danger is to betray one's parent."

sentences.zh: 無君無親，尚可立天地間哉！

translations.literal: Without ruler and without kin, how can one still stand between heaven and earth!"
translations.idiomatic: Without lord or parent, how can one face heaven and earth!"

sentences.zh: 」即遣胡深等將民兵數万往赴援，而親率精銳為之殿。

translations.literal: " He immediately sent Hu Shen and others to lead tens of thousands of militia to go to the relief, while he personally led picked troops to bring up the rear.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent Hu Shen with tens of thousands of militia to relieve the city and personally led elite troops as rearguard.

sentences.zh: 兵至婺，與大明兵甫接，即敗績而還。

translations.literal: When the army reached Wu and had just engaged the Great Ming troops, they were immediately defeated and returned.
translations.idiomatic: His force reached Wu, engaged the Ming army, was defeated at once, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時經略使李國鳳至浙東，承製拜宜孫江浙行省參知政事，階中奉大夫。

translations.literal: At that time the frontier commissioner Li Guofeng arrived in Zhedong and, by provisional appointment, appointed Yisun vice administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, with the rank of Grand Master for Court Audience.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier Commissioner Li Guofeng then arrived in Zhedong and appointed Yisun vice administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat with the rank of Grand Master for Court Audience.

sentences.zh: 明年，大明兵入處州，宜孫將數十騎走福建境上，欲圖報復，而所至人心已散，事不可復為。

translations.literal: The next year the Great Ming army entered Chuzhou; Yisun led several tens of horsemen and fled to the Fujian border, wishing to plot revenge, but wherever he went hearts were already scattered and the affair could not be revived.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Ming forces entered Chuzhou; Yisun fled to the Fujian border with a few dozen horsemen hoping to regroup, but his followers had dispersed and recovery was impossible.

sentences.zh: 歎曰：「處州，吾所守者也。

translations.literal: He sighed and said, "Chuzhou is what I guarded."
translations.idiomatic: He sighed, "Chuzhou was my charge."

sentences.zh: 今吾勢已窮，無所於往，不如還處州境，死亦為處州鬼耳！

translations.literal: Now my power is already exhausted and I have nowhere to go; better to return to the borders of Chuzhou—even in death I shall be a ghost of Chuzhou!"
translations.idiomatic: My strength is spent and I have nowhere left to go. Better to return to Chuzhou and die a ghost of that land!"

sentences.zh: 」既還，至處之慶元縣，為亂兵所害。

translations.literal: " Having returned, he reached Qingyuan County in Chu and was killed by disorderly troops.
translations.idiomatic: " On his return he reached Qingyuan County in Chuzhou and was killed by mutinous soldiers.

sentences.zh: 事聞，朝廷贈推誠宣力效節功臣、集賢大學士、榮祿大夫、上柱國，追封越國公，諡忠愍。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the court posthumously granted him Meritorious Minister for Sincerity, Proclamation of Power, and Loyal Service, Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Supreme Pillar of the State, posthumously enfeoffed him as Duke of Yue, with the posthumous name Zhongmin.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously honored him as Duke of Yue with the temple name Zhongmin and granted him the ranks of Grand Academician and Supreme Pillar of the State.

sentences.zh: 邁里古思

translations.literal: Mailigusi
translations.idiomatic: Mailigusi

sentences.zh: 邁里古思者，寧夏人也，字善卿。

translations.literal: Mailigusi was a man of Ningxia, styled Shanqing.
translations.idiomatic: Mailigusi came from Ningxia; his courtesy name was Shanqing.

sentences.zh: 至正十四年進士，授紹興路錄事司達魯花赤。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the fourteenth year of Zhizheng, he was appointed darughachi of the Shaoxing Circuit record office.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Zhizheng 14 (1354), he was appointed darughachi of the Shaoxing Circuit record office.

sentences.zh: 苗軍主將楊完者在杭，縱其軍鈔掠，莫敢誰何，民甚苦之。

translations.literal: The Miao army commander Yang Waner was at Hangzhou, letting his troops raid and plunder at will; none dared challenge them, and the people suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Miao commander Yang Waner was at Hangzhou, where his troops looted freely; no one dared resist, and the people suffered terribly.

sentences.zh: 俄有至紹興城中強奪人馬者，邁里古思擒斬數人，苗軍乃懼，不敢復至其境。

translations.literal: Before long some came into Shaoxing city forcibly seizing men and horses; Mailigusi captured and beheaded several, and the Miao army then feared and no longer dared enter his territory.
translations.idiomatic: When Miao soldiers entered Shaoxing to seize men and horses, Mailigusi captured and executed several; the Miao troops then feared to enter his jurisdiction again.

sentences.zh: 邁里古思名聲遂大振。

translations.literal: Mailigusi's fame thereupon rose greatly.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation soared.

sentences.zh: 會江南行台移治紹興，檄邁里古思為行台鎮撫，乃大募民兵，為守禦計。

translations.literal: When the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat moved its seat to Shaoxing, it issued an order appointing Mailigusi as Branch Secretariat pacifier; he then greatly recruited militia as a plan for defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat moved to Shaoxing, he was appointed its pacifier and raised a large militia for the city's defense.

sentences.zh: 處州山賊焚掠婺之永康、東陽，邁里古思提兵往擊之，與石抹宜孫約期夾攻其巢穴，山賊以平。

translations.literal: Chuzhou mountain bandits burned and plundered Yongkang and Dongyang in Wu; Mailigusi led troops to strike them, and with Shimoyisun agreed on a date for a pincer attack on their lair—the mountain bandits were thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When Chuzhou mountain rebels raided Yongkang and Dongyang in Wu Prefecture, Mailigusi marched against them and, coordinating with Shimoyisun, crushed their stronghold in a joint attack.

sentences.zh: 擢江東廉訪司經歷，仍留紹興，以兵衛台治。

translations.literal: He was promoted to director of the Jiangdong Surveillance Commission, yet remained at Shaoxing, using troops to guard the Secretariat seat.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to director of the Jiangdong Surveillance Commission, he remained at Shaoxing to guard the Secretariat with his troops.

sentences.zh: 時浙東、西郡縣多殘破，獨邁里古思保障紹興，境內晏然，民愛之如父母。

translations.literal: At the time eastern and western Zhejiang prefectures and counties were mostly ravaged; only Mailigusi secured Shaoxing, and within its borders all was tranquil; the people loved him as parents.
translations.idiomatic: While much of Zhejiang lay in ruins, Mailigusi alone kept Shaoxing secure and at peace; the people loved him as a parent.

sentences.zh: 江浙省臣乃承製授行樞密院判官，分院治紹興。

translations.literal: The Jiang-Zhe provincial ministers thereupon by provisional appointment granted him vice director of the Branch Bureau of Military Affairs, with a separate office administering Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang-Zhe authorities appointed him vice director of the Branch Bureau of Military Affairs with headquarters at Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 會方國珍遣兵侵紹興屬縣，邁里古思曰：「國珍本海賊，今既降，為大官，而復來害吾民，可乎！

translations.literal: When Fang Guozhen sent troops to invade the subordinate counties of Shaoxing, Mailigusi said, "Guozhen was originally a sea bandit; now having surrendered he holds high office, yet he comes again to harm our people—is this acceptable!"
translations.idiomatic: When Fang Guozhen sent troops against Shaoxing's counties, Mailigusi said, "Guozhen was a pirate who surrendered and received high office—how can he now prey on our people again?"

sentences.zh: 」欲率兵往問罪。

translations.literal: " He wished to lead troops to demand accountability.
translations.idiomatic: " He prepared to march against him.

sentences.zh: 先遣部將黃中取上虞，中還，請益兵。

translations.literal: He first sent his deputy commander Huang Zhong to take Shangyu; Zhong returned and requested more troops.
translations.idiomatic: He first sent Deputy Commander Huang Zhong to take Shangyu; Huang returned requesting reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 是時朝廷方倚重國珍，資其舟以運糧，而御史大夫拜住哥，與國珍素通賄賂，情好甚厚，憤邁里古思擅舉兵，恐且生事，即使人召邁里古思至其私第，與計事，至則命左右以鐵槌撾死之，斷其頭，擲廁溷中。

translations.literal: At that time the court was relying heavily on Guozhen, using his boats to transport grain, while the Censor-in-Chief Baizhuge had long exchanged bribes with Guozhen and their friendship was very close; enraged that Mailigusi had raised troops on his own authority and fearing he might cause trouble, he sent men to summon Mailigusi to his private residence to discuss affairs; when he arrived he ordered those at his side to beat him to death with iron mallets, severed his head, and threw it into a privy.
translations.idiomatic: The court then relied on Guozhen's fleet for grain transport. Censor-in-Chief Baizhuge, who was close to Guozhen through bribery, feared Mailigusi's unauthorized campaign would upset their arrangement. He summoned Mailigusi to his home, had him beaten to death with iron mallets, severed his head, and threw it into a privy.

sentences.zh: 城中民聞之，不問男女老幼，無不慟哭者。

translations.literal: When the people of the city heard of it, regardless of male or female, old or young, none failed to wail in grief.
translations.idiomatic: When the city learned of his murder, men and women, young and old, wept without exception.

sentences.zh: 黃中乃率其眾復仇，盡殺拜住哥家人及台府官員掾史，獨留拜住哥不殺，以告於張士誠，士誠乃遣其將以兵守紹興。

translations.literal: Huang Zhong then led his host to take revenge, killing all of Baizhuge's family and the officials and clerks of the Secretariat and prefectural office; he alone left Baizhuge alive, reporting the matter to Zhang Shicheng, and Shicheng then sent his generals with troops to guard Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zhong led his men in revenge, slaughtering Baizhuge's family and the Secretariat staff but sparing Baizhuge himself; he reported to Zhang Shicheng, who then sent troops to occupy Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 拜住哥尋遷行宣政院使，監察御史真童糾言：「拜住哥陰害帥臣，幾致激變，不法不忠，莫斯為甚。

translations.literal: Baizhuge was soon transferred to commissioner of the Branch Court for the Spread of Governance; investigating censor Zhen Tong impeached him, saying, "Baizhuge secretly harmed a commander and nearly caused an uprising—unlawful and disloyal, nothing exceeds this."
translations.idiomatic: Baizhuge was soon made commissioner of the Branch Court for the Spread of Governance, but Investigating Censor Zhen Tong impeached him: "Baizhuge secretly murdered a commander and nearly provoked rebellion—nothing could be more lawless or disloyal."

sentences.zh: 宜稽諸彝典，置於嚴刑。

translations.literal: He ought to be judged by the great statutes and subjected to severe punishment."
translations.idiomatic: He should be judged by statute and punished to the full extent of the law."

sentences.zh: 」於是詔削拜住哥官職，安置潮州，而邁里古思之冤始白。

translations.literal: " Thereupon an edict stripped Baizhuge of his offices and exiled him to Chaozhou, and only then was Mailigusi's wrong made clear.
translations.idiomatic: " The court stripped Baizhuge of his offices and exiled him to Chaozhou, and Mailigusi's innocence was at last acknowledged.
